claims.text: mentoring-plan.md sets a weekly thirty-minute 1-1 between mentor and newcomer; architecture-skills-checklist.md can be rated alone or together with the mentor in that 1-1.

architecture-skills-checklist.md lists fifteen kinds of document (KN1-KN15), from a requirements document to a leadership brief, each with an example file in the repository and a challenge question ('Câu phản biện để thử').
Three levels: Bậc 1 written with the template and mentor; Bậc 2 written alone, the reviewer rewrites no part; Bậc 3 defended under challenge with a driver, measurement or ADR, not liking.

Rating is by evidence: a file you wrote and what happened when others read it. So reading is not evidence, and a row with no file written has no evidence for level 1: its cell stays empty and it counts as below level 1 (lesson's reading of l.12-15).
The checklist says level 3 matters because a design that cannot be defended is a design not yet fully understood; each row's challenge question lets you test that level alone.
KN3 (ADR, example 0021) asks where the rejected option beats the chosen one and which signal would change your mind.

Choosing the next step: the lowest row picks, not the most interesting topic; a tie goes to the row the coming decision needs; STAGE.md's 'What a lesson can learn from each new place' table maps the example file to its topic.

Redo that topic's exercise on a new problem, such as a new Đơn Hàng feature, instead of rereading; the stated reason is that writing again from the start shows the weak spot more clearly than reading.

Real system: write design review and ADR for the next decision with predicted consequences; a quarter later compare with what happened, as architecture-health-review.md (checks past decisions still hold) does; re-rate after each document, not on a schedule.
The 'Bậc đạt' column of the skills table is empty in the file; the table ends at KN15.
KN6 (SLO and error budget) has example docs/design/slo.md, which names catalog-reads as a limit; in STAGE.md at stage-4 slo.md is in the row whose module is backend/capacity-and-slo.

'Khoảng trống của lộ trình' lists six topics the path left out on purpose, to learn elsewhere when a decision needs them; the first two are code-level application security and deliberately causing failures in a running system.
mentoring-plan.md 'Chọn việc tiếp theo': after each finished task, one kind of next task practises the document at the newcomer's lowest row of architecture-skills-checklist.md.

Trade-offs: following interest fits exploring, not closing a gap; rereading fits when you cannot yet say what the document holds; redoing an exercise fits levels 1-2 with no real decision coming; real decisions give slow feedback (opinion, conditioned).

Opposing view: interest keeps you studying and an abandoned plan teaches nothing; right when studying alone with no decision coming; the checklist's tie rule lets the coming decision pick (opinion, contested).

KN7 capacity plan, KN13 roadmap, KN10 design review, KN2 design doc; KN11 architecture review (multi-shop-architecture-review.md), which unlike a design review of parts still open evaluates the chosen architecture against scenarios.
The weak row is where your next document is most likely to need rewriting, so it picks the next practice (opinion, when the goal is to write the next document alone).
